content_rule: Scenery, cities, nature, harbours and squares are in. Bar, club, nightlife and adult venue cams are out (Anthony, 2026-09-17). The one exception is a stage camera whose feed carries real live music, which Anthony asked for by name the same day; those are gated to the venue's published set times so the app never parks on an empty stage. Cams that only broadcast part of the day or year are kept and given a live_window rather than rejected; see POSE-FORMAT.md.
pose_notes: pose drives the orbit-to-camera dive: lat/lng is the camera's own position, alt_m is eye height above ground, heading is degrees clockwise from north, pitch is degrees below the horizon (negative looks down), fov is vertical field of view.
lat/lng are researched to roughly the right street or beach; heading, pitch and fov are first guesses. aligned:false means nobody has matched the render to the live frame yet.
Press A in the viewer to align the current camera, then S to copy the corrected pose.

poses.format: Every camera carries pose {lat, lng, alt_m, heading, pitch, fov, aligned}, the same shape the earth-dive prototype reads, plus view, confidence and basis added here. heading is a compass bearing in degrees, 0 = north, 90 = east. pitch is degrees from horizontal, negative looking down. fov is the vertical field of view in degrees. alt_m is the eye height the dive lands at, in metres above ground.
poses.view: landscape means the camera sees a real scene with a horizon, so heading and pitch aim the landing at what is actually in frame. topdown means the camera sees a tank, a feeder, a burrow or the inside of the water, with no geographic view to match, so pitch is -89 and the dive ends looking straight down at the spot. heading is still set on those, because it decides which side the dive comes in over.
poses.confidence: high means the mounting point is published or mapped and the heading follows from geometry. medium means the position is solid but the heading is inferred. low means the operator does not publish the spot and the position is site-level or a best guess.
poses.aligned: false on all 47. No pose here has been matched against its live frame yet; that is what the prototype's A key is for.
poses.not_covered: Camera liveness and embeddability are not re-checked here; they carry over from the 2026-09-17 check in this file's check blocks.
poses.corrections: The 74 cameras added by the world thread arrived with provisional poses. Every one was checked against the real terrain model. 25 needed correcting: 12 had alt_m set to the site's elevation above sea level rather than eye height over the ground, 9 were positioned on the subject rather than at the camera, and 4 pointed away from the thing they are named after. Two of those fell in more than one group. All are corrected, each with its own basis line. One camera, the Santo Cristo chapel in Ponta Delgada, went to rejects as a static interior.

audio_notes: audio is one of: ambience (the camera's own microphone, expected to be worth hearing), music (the channel carries a music bed, a radio feed or a recitation, so the viewer keeps it silent whatever the speaker button says), unknown (not established either way).
unknown plays when the speaker button is on. Defaulting it to silent would leave most of the list mute and make the button look broken; this way the exceptions are the ones that get silenced.

These tags were assigned from what each channel is, not by listening: the session that wrote them cannot reach youtube.com, so no feed's audio has actually been heard. Shift+M in the viewer silences one camera for good and remembers it, which is how a wrong tag gets fixed.
tag_notes: Every camera carries a `tags` array: place (city, region, country, continent, aliases people type), scene (beach, skyline, waterhole, zoo), and qualities (busy, quiet, night lights, sunset-facing, always-on, has-sound).
Generated by tag.py, which rewrites the array from the camera's own fields plus a hand-written table of what no field knows. Edit tag.py, not this file.
has-sound marks cameras confirmed to carry real ambience or live music. audio: "unknown" means nobody has listened yet, so it gets no tag.
ads_notes: ads is one of: no (an institution, a public body or a non-profit, which do not run advertising on a live feed), yes (a channel whose business is the streams or the broadcast, which does), unknown (not established either way).

The viewer uses this only to order the rotation: an ad-free feed is dealt a little earlier and a monetised one a little later, and nothing is ever dropped for it. What the device has actually seen outranks this field as soon as it has seen anything.

These were assigned from what each channel is, not by watching: no session in this project can reach youtube.com, so no pre-roll has been observed from here. The viewer counts every advert it does meet (roundtrip.adseen on the device) and re-weights that camera itself, which is how a wrong guess corrects.

The only thing that removes advertising rather than ordering around it is a signed-in YouTube Premium account: an embedded player honours the viewer's own subscription. The Ads item in the action strip is that sign-in.
